websiteToolDeloadCalculator.title: Deload calculator
websiteToolDeloadCalculator.intro: Enter a lift's working weight and sets and get the deload week: how much lighter to go, how many sets to keep, how hard to push and how long it lasts.

form.weightHint: What you lift for your normal working sets.
form.sets: Working sets in a normal week
form.setsHint: Whole number, for this one exercise.

problems.weight: Enter the working weight as a number above 0 and at most {{max}}.
problems.sets: Enter the sets as a whole number from 1 to {{max}}.

results.title: Your deload week
results.weightNote: {{percent}} lighter than your working weight, rounded down to a load you can set. Keep your usual reps.
results.setsNote: Down from {{from}}: about two thirds, never fewer than one.
results.effortNote: Stop each set with about {{count}} reps still possible, so the week feels easy on purpose.
results.durationNote: Train as often as usual with lighter work, then go back to your normal loads.
results.plates: Plates on each side of the bar
results.noLighter: This is already the lightest load this equipment can make, so the weight stays. Cut the sets and push less hard instead.
results.step: One load step for this equipment is {{step}}.

table.title: Other common cuts
table.note: Musclog takes 10% or one load step, whichever is larger. The 10, 15 and 20% rows are rules of thumb, not study results. Each is rounded down to a load you can really set, so a small weight can end up lighter by more than the cut you asked for.

sections.title: How much lighter, and for how long
body: The Musclog app's deload is a cut of 10% or one load step, whichever is larger, rounded down to a weight your equipment can make and always strictly lighter than now. A lighter week then keeps about two thirds of the working sets, keeps the planned reps and aims for 4 reps in reserve. It lasts one week. All of these are Musclog product choices, not study results.

Lifters often use 10 to 20% less weight, or about a third fewer sets, for a week. Use the table for a deeper cut if the week before felt very heavy. Keep the same exercises and the same number of sessions: a deload is lighter training, not a week off.

sections.title: When a deload makes sense
body: The usual signs are the same weight feeling much heavier than a few weeks ago, missed reps you normally hit and almost no reps left in reserve. Poor sleep, stress or illness can look the same, and a deload helps with those too. If a joint hurts sharply, see a doctor or physiotherapist instead.

The app deloads one exercise on its own after two sessions in a row at the same load where you ended with nothing in reserve or missed the planned reps. It suggests a lighter week from your Weekly Review when several lifts stall. You choose whether to take it.

sections.title: What the research says
body: A 2023 consensus study of strength and physique coaches defined a deload as a period of reduced training stress meant to limit fatigue, support recovery and prepare you for later training. That is a definition, not a prescription. The numbers on this page do not come from it.

sources.bell: Bell et al. (2023), Integrating deloading into strength and physique sports training programmes: an international Delphi consensus approach (Sports Medicine - Open)
sources.zourdos: Zourdos et al. (2016), Novel resistance training-specific RPE scale measuring repetitions in reserve
